Do not accept claims to the contrary.

For anyone at Otford Medical Practice to insist that you use an online form is not legally defensible. Stating this is usually enough to get them to back down.

However, if they were to choose to debate this, feel free to cheerfully correct them on their obligations to the public.

OBLIGATION ONE

Otford Medical Practice is obligated, under the GP contract, to adhere to the NHS England patient charter. The charter states

"You can choose the way you contact your practice based on what is best for you"

and explicitly lists "Call them" as an option for how to do this.

(Source: https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/you-and-your-general-practice-english/?utm_source=chatgpt.com#what-happens-when-you-contact-your-practice-to-request-an-appointment)

OBLIGATION TWO

Otford Medical Practice is obligated by UK law to provide "reasonable adjustments" under the 2010 Equality Act. You have legal protections under this act, if you have

- a physical impairment (e.g. mobility, visual, hearing)
- a mental health condition (e.g. depression, PTSD)
- a neurodevelopmental condition (e.g. dyslexia, ADHD, autism/ASD)
- a cognitive impairment (e.g. dementia)

As such, employees of Otford Medical Practice are legally allowed to say

"We normally ask patients to complete our online form...”

but not legally allowed to say

"You must complete our online form."

(Source: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/accessibility-requirements-for-public-sector-websites-and-apps)

"If you don’t feel comfortable raising issues directly with the practice, you can contact your Integrated Care Board (ICB)"
